changelog.change: Initial entry — visit-by-visit screening table. Review against the current-year ACOG schedule before use.

summary: A visit-by-visit schedule of routine prenatal screening. Cell-free DNA is the most sensitive aneuploidy screen but is still a screen — a positive result needs diagnostic testing (CVS or amniocentesis). Start aspirin before 16 weeks if the preeclampsia screen or history warrants it.

body.text: This is a reference snapshot. Screening recommendations, cfDNA indications, and GDM cut-offs vary by institution and change over time — confirm against your current-year local protocol.

rows: First visit
Blood type / Rh + antibody screen, CBC, rubella IgG, hepatitis B surface antigen, HIV, RPR/VDRL, gonorrhoea & chlamydia, hepatitis C, varicella IgG, urinalysis + culture, Pap if due
TSH if symptomatic or high-risk; TB testing if risk; early 1-h GCT if BMI ≥ 25 with risk factors
10–13 weeks
Combined first-trimester screen (nuchal translucency + PAPP-A + free β-hCG); OR cell-free DNA (preferred by many for aneuploidy — screens T21, T18, T13, sex-chromosome aneuploidies)
Offer diagnostic testing (CVS 10–13 wk, amniocentesis ≥ 15 wk) after a positive screen or for a structural anomaly
11–16 weeks
Preeclampsia risk assessment (history ± MAP, uterine-artery Doppler, PAPP-A/PlGF)
High risk → aspirin 81–150 mg/day started before 16 weeks
15–20 weeks
Quad screen (AFP, hCG, uE3, inhibin A) if no cfDNA; MSAFP alone for neural-tube defects
Elevated AFP: neural-tube defect, abdominal-wall defect, multiple gestation, or wrong dates
18–22 weeks
Detailed fetal anatomy ultrasound
Cervical length if a preterm-birth risk factor
24–28 weeks
1-h 50 g glucose challenge (→ 3-h GTT if ≥ 140, some use ≥ 130); repeat CBC; Rh-negative unsensitised → anti-D at 28 wk (RhoGAM 300 mcg)
35–37 weeks
GBS vaginal–rectal swab; confirm fetal presentation
GBS-positive (or bacteriuria this pregnancy, or a prior GBS-affected infant) → intrapartum penicillin G
